Must have access to reliable transportation.
Effort outside of the normal 40-hour workweek may occasionally be required.
Fiscal & Calendar Year End closing is a critical business period during which vacation requests may not be approved.
Proven experience in high volume, mission critical data processing using a PC with fast and accurate data entry and typing skills with a minimum of 60 WPM.

Demonstrated experience in updating and utilizing a mission critical database to enter, maintain, or to relay information in comprehensive manner. Experience in use of a fundraising/donor database preferred.

Demonstrated experience and knowledge in general computerized applications: appropriate coding techniques, formatting, and terminology; ability to search for and compile data; experience with Excel and Word.
Demonstrated experience in working with interruptions and fluctuating priorities.

Advancement Services within Advancement is responsible for providing gift policy and infrastructure support in fundraising; processing, accounting for, and stewarding all charitable gifts to both UC San Diego and the UC San Diego Foundation; and overseeing the operations of the legally separate incorporated 501c3 charity, the UC San Diego Foundation.

These areas not only represent the highest risk fiduciary operations in Advancement and one of the highest risks on the campus, but they are also highly unique on the campus. No other campus unit has the delegated authority to process and receipt gifts or directly manage financial investments. The campus foundations are legally separate and have a separate fiduciary board of trustees. Accordingly, due to the complex nature of operations and oversight for a foundation, the fiduciary risk, and the magnitude of funds involved, there are reputational, legal, IRS, accounting, and donor relations requirements that must be adhered to.

Functional areas of Advancement Services include UC San Diego Foundation Board Operations and Management; Gift & Foundation Accounting, and Gift Services, Investment Operations, and the Office of Gift Policy Administration and Donor/Fund Stewardship.

The Gift Revenue Records Coordinator plays a crucial role in handling donations, maintaining records, and ensuring the accuracy of gift-related data. This position requires attention to detail, strong organizational skills, and the ability to handle sensitive information with discretion.
Demonstrated professional telephone manners, exercising good manners and grammar during phone calls.

Ability to analyze diverse correspondence/documentation to insure complete and accurate information has been received, and application of appropriate updates is made.
Ability to sustain careful attention to repetitive detail for long periods of time with an emphasis on accuracy.
Resourcefulness in finding appropriate solutions to problems. Ability to present alternatives and follow through to ensure effective changes.
Good math ability to comprehend and perform standard applications.
Ability to work independently and complete tasks. Proven ability to exercise good judgement in daily work. Proven ability to take direction.
Demonstrated skill in explaining financial and database functions to outside personnel.
Demonstrated skill in organizing, analyzing, managing time, setting priorities, and meeting deadlines for multiple tasks.
Excellent customer service and interpersonal skills, with the ability to communicate effectively with individuals in a diplomatic professional manner.
Demonstrated ability to project a helpful, cheerful manner when dealing with visitors, callers and colleagues.
Ability to maintain confidentiality and use discretion in handling of sensitive issues of concern.

Foster the best possible working and learning environment. UCSD strives to maintain a climate of fairness, cooperation, and professionalism. Demonstrated ability to understand and adhere to UCSD Principles of Community while supporting and guiding others in the Advancement Services mission.
